ai.description: The Chitral gecko reaches 50 mm in snout-vent length. It is grey-brown with dark transverse bands and a white underside. Key features include granular dorsal scales and a slender, unsegmented tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Mediodactylus walli* is uniquely distinguished by the presence of 12–14 longitudinal rows of enlarged, trihedral tubercles on its back, which are more numerous than in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Chitral gecko inhabits arid, rocky slopes and boulder-strewn terrain within the Hindu Kush mountains, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Chitral gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects across the rocky crevices and stone walls of its arid mountain habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Mediodactylus walli* is oviparous, laying a single hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs during the warmer months, typically from spring through summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Mediodactylus walli* is found in the Hindu Kush mountains of northern Pakistan (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) at elevations typically ranging from 1,000 to 2,500 meters.
